q: Which reading of these two machine numbers is correct: a Roper Whitney 816 hand brake and a Wysong 1652 power shear?
opts: 816 brake: 8 ft long, 16 ga max | 1652 shear: 16 ga max, 52" long
816 brake: 8 ga max, 16 ft long | 1652 shear: 16 ft long, 52 ga max
816 brake: 8 ft long, 16 ga max | 1652 shear: 16 ft long, 52 ga max
816 brake: 8 ga max, 16" long | 1652 shear: 16 ga max, 52" long
evidence: Manufacturer: https://roperwhitney.com/our-products/816-hand-brake/ — 'This machine has a bending capacity of 16 gauge up to 8 feet long', bending length 97 in, 16 ga mild steel. Wysong 1652: https://surplusrecord.com/listing/16-gauge-x-4-wysong-h-1652-hydraulic-power-squaring-shear-52-cut-l-3-hp-58-spm-1145183/ ('16 gauge x 4' Wysong H-1652 ... 52" cut'), https://www.machinetools.com/en/for-sale/751248-wysong-1652-power-squaring-shears-gauge/spec_sheet; same naming by Jet: FS-1652J '52" x 16 Gauge Foot Shear' (https://www.penntoolco.com/jet-foot-shear-52-x-16-gauge-capacity-fs-1652j-87-112-061/). Wysong's own parts-manual model list (https://wysong.us/resources/parts-manuals/) has the same gauge+inches family: 1052, 1252, 1452, 1472, 1096, 1460. Class 11/19 transcript 12:32:07-12:32:22: brake 'length first, then gauge', shear 'flip, gauge then length'.

Bend heavy plate into identical angles

opts: Ounces per square foot
Pounds per square foot
Gauge number
Thickness in mils
evidence: Class 11/19 transcript 12:43:55-12:44:07: lead 'gauged by a weight ... pounds per square foot. Whereas copper is ounces per square foot'. Thickness check in python with copper density 8.96 g/cm³ = 0.3237 lb/in³: 16 oz → 0.0215", 20 oz → 0.0268" (industry tables: 0.0216", 0.0270"). q: Sheet metal that is approximately 1/8" thick is about ____ gauge.
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:15:49-12:16:41: instructor: 1/8 = 10 ga on the test, 11 ga more accurate in real life. MSG thicknesses from knowledge/06 §9 table; differences computed in python. Same fact as bank MON-19 (16 ga about 1/16, twice as thick -> 10), different wording as the instructor asked it.

q: A hand (leaf) brake has a capacity of 816. What does that mean?
opts: It bends up to 8 gauge mild steel, 16 feet long
It bends up to 16 gauge mild steel, 8 feet long
It bends up to 16 gauge stainless steel, 8 feet long
It bends up to 8 gauge mild steel, 16 inches long
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:30:43-12:32:22: instructor: brake = length first, then gauge; shear flipped (gauge, then length); numbers are flip-flop. Manufacturers (web, 11/19): Tin Knocker TK-816 leaf brake, Capacity 16 Ga, Bend Length 8'1" (penntoolco.com/tin-knocker-8ft-leaf-brake-tk-816); Tennsmith HBU48-16: mild steel 16 ga, bending length 48-1/4" (penntoolco.com/tennsmith-bench-model-hand-brake-16-ga-hbu48-16); Tennsmith HBU72-16 and TK-816 vendors: 16 ga mild / 20 ga stainless. Course: brake capacity = max mild steel (bank Y2W3M-53).

q: A foot squaring shear is rated 1652. What does that mean?
opts: It cuts up to 16 gauge mild steel, 52" long
It cuts 16 ft long sheets up to 52 gauge
It cuts up to 16 gauge stainless steel, 52" long
It cuts sheets up to 52" wide in any gauge
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:30:43-12:32:22 (shear = gauge first, then length). Web 11/19: Tin Knocker TN-1652 'Capacity: 16 Ga Mild Steel', 'Shearing Length: 52"' (penntoolco.com/tin-knocker-foot-operated-shear-tn-1652); JET FS-1652J '52" x 16 Gauge Foot Shear' (wurthlac / homedepot listings); Wysong 1072 = 10 ga x 72", Wysong 1652 = 16 ga; Wysong #1016 power squaring shear: 'Gauge: 16', 'Length: 10.0' ft (surplusrecord listing 811610). So power shears 1010/1016/1025 are length-first; T90-80 (816 power shear, 12 ga -> No) and T90-67 (No) keys stand.

q: When you solve a right triangle on the calculator (X = run, Y = rise), which side is the Y value?
opts: The side that runs to and from the angle you are working from
The side opposite the angle you are working from
The hypotenuse, across from the 90° corner
Always the vertical side, whatever angle you work from
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:18:24-12:19:02: instructor: Y is always opposite the relative angle, X runs to and from the angle; values change with the angle asked. Numbers: python, 13.67 cos/sin 52.4 = 8.3407 / 10.8306 (same data as T90-55).

q: Before you can solve the pipe length and overall length of an offset made with two equal elbows, which three values do you need?
opts: Throat radius, heel radius and duct gauge
Duct width, duct depth and overall length
Centerline radius, elbow degree and the offset
Pipe length, overall length and elbow degree
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:19:58-12:20:44: instructor: three things needed: centerline radius, elbow degree, offset. Formulas: knowledge/03 §3; example = formula sheet p15 (18x20, R1'-6" throat, 30°, offset 145 − 98 = 47): python K 7.2346, 2K 14.4693, PL 79.5307, L 95.8756 (checked by arcs), same as 03 Type B and Y2W5Y-63.

q: In the first part of the two-elbow offset formula, K = centerline radius × tan of an angle. Which angle do you use?
opts: The full elbow degree
Twice the elbow degree
90° minus the elbow degree
Half the elbow degree
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:20:44-12:20:45: instructor: for the first part of the formula you need half the elbow degree; people enter the full degree and get the pipe length wrong. Python: 27 tan 15 = 7.2346; 27 tan 30 = 15.5885; PL 79.5307 vs 62.8231 (difference 16.7076). Method knowledge/03 §3 step 5.

q: Which set of length names is correct for a duct section with S&D connections?
opts: Layout = shear length, Net = working length, Gross = connection length
Layout = working length, Net = shear length, Gross = connection length
Layout = working length, Net = connection length, Gross = shear length
Layout = connection length, Net = shear length, Gross = working length
evidence: Review class 11/19, 12:21:03-12:21:29: instructor: layout = working length, net = connection (drive to drive), gross = shear. Course sheet 2J / knowledge/06 §2 (Net = Layout + 1, Gross = Layout + 2); examples = T90-39 (27 -> 25) and CLS-12 (20 -> 19 / 21). Term options kept in English in Russian because the question tests the English names.
